patch.value: Scale fixtures vary only in size: the sole synthetic workspace generator hardcodes population shape, so the million-item tier is eleven simulated days deep with one history entry per item

The scale benchmark generator at scripts/bench/scale-workspace.mjs is the only synthetic workspace producer in the repository and it exposes exactly two knobs, items and seed. Every other dimension of corpus shape is a hardcoded constant: parent index is the item index minus index modulo twenty, giving a hierarchy of exactly depth two with fan-out exactly twenty; timestamps are the 2026-01-01 base plus one second per item, so the million-item tier spans 11.6 days of simulated project time while the roadmap promises millions of items spanning decades; each item receives exactly one history entry, where the live corpus carries 41,231 entries over 2,204 streams for a mean of 18.7, a median of 14, a p90 of 33 and a maximum of 922, meaning every history-path measurement at the top tier is understated by roughly nineteen times; dependency rows use only two kinds, related on every third index and blocks on every eleventh, where the live graph uses ten kinds including 2,069 implements, 426 blocked_by, 236 discovered_from, 150 verifies and 56 supersedes; there are zero comments, notes and learnings; there is one constant author where the live corpus has 477 spellings; and there are no custom types, statuses, fields, applied profiles or extension-contributed fields. This is a conformance gap against pm-m2il's own fixture criterion, which requires empty and seconds-old scratch projects, representative medium histories, deep and cyclic typed graphs, multi-decade event streams and disconnected archives alongside the size tiers - only the size tiers are producible today. It is also the missing instrument for roadmap horizon Q, which asks which of the product's fitted constants travel to other corpora: that question cannot be answered while only one corpus shape can be synthesized.

Corpus shape is a declared, versioned specification naming hierarchy depth and fan-out distribution, age span and density, history entries per item, annotation volume, edge-kind mix, author cardinality, and schema customization; The generator produces every fixture shape that pm-m2il's criterion names, including a deep typed graph, a multi-decade age span, a disconnected archive, and a seconds-old scratch workspace, each reproducible from a seed and a shape name; Generated corpora report their measured shape so a benchmark result is attributable to a population rather than to a size alone, and a shape whose measured profile drifts from its declaration fails; At least one published scale, retrieval, and context number is re-measured across two shapes at the same item count, and any constant whose behaviour differs by more than a declared margin is recorded as corpus-fitted rather than universal; The shape specification is reachable from the public SDK so downstream users, evaluation episodes, and domain packs generate their own populations without copying the benchmark script
A declared corpus-shape specification drives generation, so scale, retrieval, context and history claims can be measured across populations that differ in shape as well as size.
Only item count and seed are variable; hierarchy depth, fan-out, age spread, history depth, edge-kind mix, annotation volume, author diversity and schema customization are compiled-in constants.
